title: Scheduling concept — synthetic interview report
summary: These two simulated roles suggest testing change visibility and approval clarity before assuming teams need a new scheduling system. No real users were interviewed.

findings.statement: For the stable-rota employee, a lightweight notification may be sufficient without adopting another app.
limitations: The stable rota is a constructed assumption, not an observed user segment.

findings.statement: The simulated supervisor values approval clarity but rejects duplicate schedule entry.
limitations: The frequency and cost of approval confusion remain unknown.

next_steps: Observe how a real team handles one schedule change, with consent.
Ask whether a message linked to the existing sheet already solves missed changes.
Test a single-source-of-truth prototype with an actual approver before discussing pricing.
limitations: All personas and interview responses are synthetic; this is not demand validation.
Two deliberately contrasting scenarios do not estimate the prevalence of either workflow.
No willingness-to-pay or time-saving measurement was collected.
